ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #2
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a describing word
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only an action
   D. Only a joining word

2. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.

3. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. quickly
   C. happiness
   D. run

4. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.

5. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goed
   C. goes
   D. going

6. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.

7. When practising Play: Structure and Setting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Play: Structure and Setting.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Play: Structure and Setting.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Play: Structure and Setting.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Play: Structure and Setting.

8. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.

9. When practising Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.

10. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.

11. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.

12. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. No full stops
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Oral Reports: News and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 15.2.1 Reading Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in use 15.3.1 Sentences- 15.3.1.1 Imperative – commands, requests 15.3.1 and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — A person, place, thing, or idea

2. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.

3. D — run

4. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.

5. A — went

6. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.

7. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Play: Structure and Setting.

8. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.

9. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.

10. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.

11. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.

12. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Oral Reports: News; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 15.2.1 Reading Fluency; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in use 15.3.1 Sentences- 15.3.1.1 Imperative – commands, requests 15.3.1; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
